Question: In counting \(n\) colored balls, some red and some black, it was found that \(49\) of the first \(50\) counted were red. Thereafter, \(7\) out of every \(8\) counted were red. If, in all, \(90\%\) or more of the balls counted were red, the maximum value of \(n\) is:
Solution:
Method 1: Assuming an exact overall proportion

Assume that exactly \(\frac78\) of all balls counted after the first \(50\) are red. Their red-to-black ratio is then \(7:1\), so write their counts as \(7m\) red and \(m\) black, where \(m\) is a nonnegative integer. Thus
\[
n=50+8m,
\qquad \text{red count}=49+7m.
\]
The requirement that at least \(90\%\) are red becomes
\[
49+7m\ge\frac9{10}(50+8m).
\]
Multiplying by \(10\) and simplifying gives
\[
490+70m\ge450+72m,
\qquad m\le20.
\]
At \(m=20\), there are \(210\) balls, of which \(189\) are red, exactly \(90\%\). Under this exact-proportion reading, the maximum is therefore \(\boxed{210}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).

This calculation requires the stated proportion to apply to the entire later count, rather than only to completed groups of eight.

Method 2: Allowing an incomplete final group

Suppose instead that each complete group of eight balls after the first \(50\) contains seven red balls, and counting may stop partway through another group. Write the later count uniquely as \(8k+r\), where \(k\ge0\) is an integer and \(0\le r\le7\).

The complete groups contain \(7k\) red balls. Even if all \(r\) balls in the final partial group are red, the total red count is at most \(49+7k+r\). Therefore a necessary condition for reaching \(90\%\) is
\[
49+7k+r\ge\frac9{10}(50+8k+r).
\]
This simplifies to
\[
2k\le40+r\le47.
\]
Hence \(k\le23\), and every allowed count satisfies
\[
n=50+8k+r\le50+8(23)+7=241.
\]
This bound is attainable. After the first \(50\) balls, use \(23\) repetitions of seven red balls followed by one black ball, then seven more red balls. Every complete group of eight has seven red balls; this repeating pattern also satisfies the condition for every consecutive eight-ball window among the later balls. The total is \(241\) balls with
\[
49+23(7)+7=217
\]
red balls. Since \(2170>9(241)=2169\), more than \(90\%\) are red.

Under this reading the maximum is \(\boxed{241}\), which is absent from the choices. Thus an exact overall proportion, or a requirement to finish a complete group, is needed to force choice B.
